purpose: Routes that have been closed, with the reason each fails. A proposal that matches a closed lane must either cite new information that defeats the stated obstruction, or be rejected without spending a Lean build on it.

closure_kinds.circular: an exact identity that restates the target in other notation; proving it is proving the target
closure_kinds.lossy: the route is sound but discards more than the target can afford
closure_kinds.ceiling: the mechanism is real but its best case is provably weaker than the target

lanes.title: Bound the wheel residual by summing separately bounded square blocks
lanes.claim: Per-block bounds on Delta_j, summed, control the pinned wheel residual R_k.
lanes.obstruction: Only the signed sum telescopes. sum_{j<=J} Delta_j = R_k(X_J) - R_k(X_0), so replacing it by sum_j |Delta_j| discards exactly the cancellation being sought. Measured loss over mu-sieved data: 29.7x at J=64, 660x at J=256, 67.5x at J=1024, against sqrt(J) = 8.0, 16.0, 32.0. Over a full primorial block J is astronomically larger.

evidence.lean_note: The module header states this directly: an absolute-value sum over the blocks loses a full square-root factor.

lanes.what_would_reopen: A bound on the SIGNED consecutive sums that does not pass through per-block absolute values. Note that such a bound is the wheel residual bound itself, so this is circular unless it supplies independent correlation information about adjacent Delta_j.

lanes.title: Differentiate the square-root smooth/transport prefix decomposition
lanes.claim: Differencing M(X_n) = A_n - T_n exposes a new cross-n cancellation mechanism.
lanes.obstruction: The decomposition is at the PREFIX level (squarePrefixMertens_eq_squareRootSmooth_sub_transport), so the increment is Delta A_n - Delta T_n. The reclassification term created when the square-root cutoff advances appears in both increments with the same sign and cancels identically, returning Delta A_n - Delta T_n = Delta_n. The derivative removes the moving-cutoff mechanism rather than exposing it.
lanes.what_would_reopen: Nothing at the level of the raw (A,T) pair. The lifetime decomposition M(X_t) = L + Z + D is the productive replacement, since it discharges two of three terms unconditionally.

lanes.title: Bound the survivor via residue energy and finite Cauchy-Schwarz
lanes.claim: |Z|^2 <= s (D + C) with negative cross-cofactor covariance C cancelling the diagonal D delivers an RH-scale survivor bound for some modulus schedule.
lanes.obstruction: C is indeed negative at every modulus tested, but the fibre split and the prime-face toggle are governed by the same object: the square-unit subgroup mod s. For s | 24 every unit has q^2 = 1, so u = const - c^2 is a FUNCTION of c, the split is Z re-bucketed, and proving the energy small is proving the survivor bound. Raising s makes the fibres informative (30.6 fibres per cofactor at s=10080) but degrades V/D from 1e-4 to 0.61 while the factor s enters the bound. At t=600, |Z| = 27 against a target of t = 600, yet sqrt(sV) never falls below 1642 at any modulus tested.
lanes.caveats: t <= 600 (X_t ~ 3.6e5) is small and sqrt(sV)/t IS falling with t at s=12 (4.68 -> 2.74 across t=200..600). The closure is on the STRUCTURE - degeneracy trades against the Cauchy factor - not on the numerics alone.
lanes.what_would_reopen: Applying the toggle pairing BEFORE passing to residues: cancel matched (c, c*ell) sources directly in Z = sum_c -mu(c) K(c), leaving the boundary set {c : c*ell*q > X_t} as the unpaired remainder. That keeps the mechanism and never introduces s, so neither the degeneracy nor the Cauchy factor applies.
lanes.reopener_outcome: Tried on 2026-08-09 and carried out; it terminates in the lane 'canonical-orientation-split' below. Pairing before residues is exactly the far-upper survivor route, and RHLean/Proof/SurvivorFarUpperRigidity.lean proves the fixed-q fibre is then the FULL negative reciprocal Mertens prefix -M(floor(X_t/q)) with no unpaired-boundary saving at all. The remainder set {c : c*ell*q > X_t} is empty in the far range, so the pairing cancels nothing there.

lanes.title: Split the square-root smooth mass by canonical orientation (c < q against q <= c) and bound the matched born-smooth / transport object
lanes.claim: squareRootMatchedBornSmoothTransport R = bornSmooth R - transport R is the residual carrying the large cancellation, so an RH-scale bound on it (equivalently on bornSmooth + farUpperSurvivor, which differs from it by the elementary 7R root strip) delivers the RH-scale Mertens bound.
lanes.obstruction: The orientation split leaves exactly one region uncancelled, and that region is a pi-weighted Mertens sum of true order R^(3/2)/log R, a full quarter power of X = R^2-1 above the X^(1/2+eps) target. Writing q = P+(m) and c = m/q, the positive-orientation region c < q <= R collapses in closed form to squareRootPositiveSmoothMass R = -sum_{q<=R prime} M(q-1) = -sum_{c<R} mu(c)*(pi(R)-pi(c)), and M(R^2-1) = positiveSmooth R + matched R. Summation by parts turns positiveSmooth into an INTEGRAL of M against dpi: integration is a smoothing that removes precisely the sign oscillation the target needs. Under RH the explicit formula gives int_1^R M(t)dt = sum_rho R^(rho+1)/(rho(rho+1)zeta'(rho)) + O(1), every term of modulus exactly R^(3/2)/|rho(rho+1)zeta'(rho)|, so no cancellation among zeros can push it below R^(3/2-o(1)). Hence matched R = M(R^2-1) - positiveSmooth R is itself of order R^(3/2)/log R. The route is self-defeating: if |matched| << R^(1+eps) were proved, then |M(R^2-1)| >= |positiveSmooth| - |matched| would be Omega(R^(3/2-eps)) = Omega(X^(3/4-eps)), which DISPROVES RH.

measured.closed_form_check: positiveSmooth R = -sum_{q<=R} M(q-1) verified against the literal largest-prime-factor definition for every R = 2..300, together with smooth = bornSmooth + positiveSmooth, M(R^2-1) = smooth - transport, and M(R^2-1) = positiveSmooth + matched
measured.growth_of_positiveSmooth: running max over R <= 5.37e8; fitted exponent 1.4440 on the last 8 octaves against the predicted 1.5 - 1/log R = 1.4502 at that R
measured.normalised_band: |positiveSmooth| * log R / R^1.5 stays in [0.0079, 0.0202] for R in [1e5, 5.37e8] - flat over four decades
measured.ratio_to_R: |positiveSmooth|/R rises from 0.32 at R=128 to 18.96 at R=5.37e8, i.e. it diverges away from the R^(1+eps) target
measured.mechanism_check: positiveSmooth R / (-int_2^R M(t)/log t dt) = 0.641, 0.748, 0.903, 0.963, 0.976, 1.005 at R = 1e3..1e8: the object IS the smoothed integral of M
measured.integral_carries_full_power: running max of |sum_{n<=R} M(n)| has fitted exponent 1.5606 on the last 8 octaves to R = 6.7e7

lanes.caveats: The Omega(R^(3/2-eps)) statement for the integral of M is the explicit-formula consequence under RH with simple zeros; the numerics are what pin the constant and the exponent in the computed range. No Lean build was available in the closing session, so nothing here is machine checked.

variants_covered.native_moebius_atom_population: The RH_Lean #305 square-shell reformulation writes Matched_R = sum_{m in U_R} mu(m) over an explicit geometric atom set, with U_R = region1 (born-smooth, q<=c) union region3 (high, q>R), and proposes the balance |Matched_R|^2 <<_eps R^eps D_R with D_R = #squarefree in U_R <= R^2-1. That coordinate is a genuine improvement - it carries the native Moebius weight mu(cq) = -mu(c) with no pi-Li centering anywhere, so it is free of the Route B contamination - but the OBJECT is this lane's object, and the proposed balance is refuted, not open. D_R <= R^2 makes the balance equivalent to |Matched_R| << R^(1+eps); combined with the verified identity matched = M(R^2-1) - positiveSmooth and the measured positiveSmooth ~ R^(3/2)/log R, it forces |M(R^2-1)| = Omega(X^(3/4-eps)) and therefore disproves RH. U_R is defined by excluding region2, and region2 IS positiveSmooth - the monotone pi-weighted Mertens sum carrying the X^(3/4) pathology. Encouraging numerics on this variant (dyadic max |Matched|^2/D_R decreasing: 1.259, 1.037, 0.690, 0.606, 0.786 for R up to 3162) are pre-asymptotic; using measured positiveSmooth and D_R ~ 0.6R^2 the ratio is about 1.7 at R=1e6, 74 at R=1e8 and 599 at R=5.37e8. The exact lifetime interval cq < R^2 <= 2cq with L(c,q)=max(c+1,floor(sqrt(cq))+1), U(c,q)=min(q-1,floor(sqrt(2cq))) and its LifetimeOverlapKernel pairing remain sound and reusable; only the diagonal balance is refuted.
variants_covered.scalar_cofactor_covariance: Collapsing each fibre to P_R(c) before the q-sum gives a rank-one Gram and creates no geometry. Correctly rejected upstream.

lanes.what_would_reopen: Nothing at the level of the (bornSmooth, transport) pair or its far-upper survivor rewriting, since the obstruction is a lower bound on an object both forms contain. A split of the smooth mass whose uncancelled region is NOT a monotone-weighted Mertens sum would be a different lane. The invariant that has predicted every closure recorded here: a decomposition survives only if no piece is a monotone-weighted Moebius sum.

lanes.title: Attack the signed combined object C^PNT - 2 E^rec as a route to the H_{k,n} bound
lanes.claim: The PNT-centered coordinates expose favourable signed structure, so attacking C - 2E directly is progress on H_{k,n}.
lanes.obstruction: C - 2E is H_{k,n} by construction, not a new object. The centering operator Z is linear and M = (allPlus - 2*Bulk) - 2*Err, so Z[M] = Z[allPlus - 2 Bulk] - 2 Z[Err] = C - 2E identically; the repository's own theorem primorialMinimalSquareWheelNonzeroResponse_eq_mertensCenter already gives H = Z[M]. Hence C = H + 2E is an identity, and the pair of obligations {|C| << s, |E| << s} is EQUIVALENT to {|H| << s, |E| << s}, which is strictly stronger than the target {|H| << s}. The coordinate change therefore cannot reduce the difficulty; it can only relocate it. The observed C/E correlation reported as favourable is forced by that identity rather than being independent evidence: with C = H + 2E and |H| comparable to |2E|, positive correlation of C with E is automatic.

measured.identity_check: C - 2E = M(x) reproduced to floating tolerance at every x on a 240-point log grid from 1e4 to 1e8
measured.correlations: corr(C, 2E) = +0.8809, corr(M, 2E) = -0.9544, corr(C, M) = -0.6994 over the grid
measured.no_reduction: |C|/|M| has median 1.296 and only 34.6 percent of grid points have |C| < |M|; max|C|/sqrt(x) = 0.4095 against max|M|/sqrt(x) = 0.4045. Neither piece is systematically smaller than the target.

lanes.caveats: This closes the coordinate change as a REDUCTION, not the reciprocal-interval representation of E^rec, which is a genuine object and is recorded as still open under not_closed below.
lanes.what_would_reopen: An independent bound on the PNT-corrected comb C that does not route through M - i.e. combinatorial control of allPlus - 2*Bulk proved without assuming the Mertens bound. That would make the split a real reduction rather than a relabelling.

lanes.title: Divisor-band cancellation of the prime-by-prime correction (all-minus-one start, corrected prime by prime, bands d = floor(x/q))
lanes.claim: Starting every site at -1 and correcting prime by prime, the bands d = floor(x/q) cancel against each other, so the divisor-band structure supplies the cancellation for free and yields the Mertens bound.
lanes.obstruction: The band bulk does reindex onto the harmonic Moebius sum, but ONLY up to a finite boundary term, and that boundary is the whole difficulty. With S_D = sum_{d<=D} M(d)/(d(d+1)) and A_D = sum_{n<=D} mu(n)/n, finite Abel summation over the telescoping 1/d - 1/(d+1) gives S_D = sum_{n<=D} mu(n)(1/n - 1/(D+1)), i.e. the EXACT identity S_D = A_D - M(D)/(D+1). The formal infinite calculation sum_{d>=1} M(d)/(d(d+1)) = sum_{n>=1} mu(n)/n = 0 silently discards M(D)/(D+1); making that boundary vanish is already PNT-strength. Worse at the target rate: requiring A_D = O(D^(-1/2+eps)) forces M(D)/(D+1) = O(D^(-1/2+eps)), i.e. M(D) = O(D^(1/2+eps)) - the boundary term literally regenerates the original Mertens problem. So the mechanism transforms the problem into 'weighted band bulk = harmonic Moebius sum + Mertens boundary' rather than solving any part of it.
lanes.unification: This is the SAME 1/log^2 lane as the added-prime Euler-density ceiling recorded under not_closed. Both arrive at 1/log^2 from opposite directions: the added-prime lever because alpha_q ~ 1.2/q in the tail sums to log log Q, and the divisor bands because the zeroth-order band cancellation is exactly sum mu(n)/n, which is PNT and no more. Divisor-band cancellation and Euler-density cancellation are one lane, not two.

measured.identity_exact: S_D = A_D - M(D)/(D+1) verified in exact rational arithmetic for EVERY D = 1..3000, zero mismatches
measured.table: A_D - S_D equals M(D)/(D+1) to all printed digits at D = 10, 1e2, 1e3, 1e4, 1e5, 1e6, 1e7
measured.band_weights: band d has weight M(d) and population pi(I_d) ~ x/(d(d+1)log(x/d)); the d=2 band (q in (x/3,x/2]) contributes exactly zero since M(2)=0, and d=1 (q > x/2) needs no correction at all
measured.extra_band_cancellation: |S_D| decays faster than |A_D| (2.18e-6 against 1.02e-4 at D=1e7) because A_D ~ M(D)/(D+1) to within a few percent and S_D is the residue between them. Suggestive of genuine additional cancellation in the band coordinate, but it is a difference of two nearly equal quantities over only four decades - not a claim.

lanes.caveats: The next-order heuristic T ~ -x/log^2 x, obtained by expanding 1/log(x/d) and inserting sum mu(n) log n / n = -1, gives the right sign and magnitude (measured T = -3.56e5 against -x/log^2 x = -2.95e5 at x = 1e8) but is NOT established as a uniform asymptotic here: promoting it requires controlling the truncation and the weighted Moebius remainder, not merely substituting the formal identity. Treat it as a heuristic only.
lanes.what_would_reopen: Control of the Mertens boundary M(D)/(D+1) at rate D^(-1/2+eps) obtained independently of the Mertens bound itself. Absent that, the reindexing is an exact restatement.

not_closed.note: Recorded so the distinction is not lost. The added-prime contraction is real but its unweighted form has a ceiling: the observed per-prime ratios are exactly (p-1)/(p+1), the pure density factor, with no arithmetic gain, and prod_p (p-1)/(p+1) decays like 1/log^2 rather than like a power. In the k=20..40 band the residual runs up to 1.88x WORSE than independent behaviour. This constrains the mechanism to the centered object H_{k,n} rather than raw partial Moebius; it does not close a lane.

reciprocal_d_family.status: open, and the measured mechanism is now identified
reciprocal_d_family.note: The reciprocal-interval family E^rec = sum_d M(d) * (pi(I_d) - LiMass(I_d)) over the D = floor(x/y) ~ sqrt(x) fibres does exhibit square-root cancellation across d, and that cancellation is exactly what carries the termwise bound down to the target. Measured on a 240-point log grid to x = 1e8: sum_d |E_d| grows with exponent 0.678 (sub-range fits 0.635, 0.648, 0.706, 0.677 - robustly ABOVE the 0.5 target, so termwise absolute values cannot close, confirming CURRENT_PROOF_ROUTE section 6), while the signed |E^rec| fits exponent 0.51 and tracks sum_d|E_d|/sqrt(D) with median ratio 1.428 and log-log correlation 0.777. The median saving over the triangle bound is 24.9x at these scales, against a required saving of about x^0.18. So the answer to 'why does the combined signed operator save roughly X^(1/2)' is: square-root cancellation over the d-fibres, with essentially no margin. What this does NOT do is move the target, for the reason recorded in lane pnt-reciprocal-coordinate-change.
